Meet Hiroyuki Kimiduka↗MOBARA, CHIBA / CATERING ACROSS JAPAN
THE PERSON BEHIND OTTO

A chef.
A connector of people.

From his restaurant in Mobara, Chiba, to tables across Japan, OTTO’s owner-chef Hiroyuki Kimiduka brings more than food. He creates opportunities for people to gather, talk and connect—with cooking at the heart of it all.

OWNER CHEF君塚 博幸HIROYUKI KIMIDUKA
01THE BEGINNING↗02THE CONNECTION↗03BEYOND THE TABLE↗
01 / THE BEGINNING

A new chapter.
At forty-one.

Until the age of forty, Kimiduka worked as an employed chef. His hotel career included the dual roles of chef and general manager, shaping both the food and the experience around it.

At forty-one, he became independent. At OTTO, that experience now lives in two settings: the restaurant and catering. The thread connecting them is the same—cooking for the people in front of him.

02 / THE CONNECTION

Turn eight sideways.
See the possibilities.

Otto means “eight” in Italian. On its side, the number becomes the symbol for infinity. Kimiduka sees himself at its crossing point, bringing people together through food.

He describes his approach as a kind of wholehearted, well-meaning involvement in people’s lives. Whether at the restaurant’s counter or a catering event, he values being close to the people he cooks for.

03 / BEYOND THE TABLE

Sharing food.
Inspiring the next generation.

Kimiduka’s work also takes him into schools. As a guest instructor, he shares the importance of eating well and thinking carefully about the information we receive about food.

He now visits elementary, junior high and high schools in Mobara, bringing work-experience sessions to students. Food becomes another way to connect—with young people discovering the world of work.

∞
THE STORY CONTINUES

Wherever we cook,
people come first.

Kimiduka wants to take catering beyond Chiba to more places across Japan, while continuing to run his restaurant. Serving a dish, hearing a response and taking that conversation into the next meal—this is where OTTO begins.

Enquiries about school visits and work-experience sessions are welcome by phone.
